text:
maya: Quick heads-up — major pilot prospect (CuraTech) says they require data-residency assurances (EU-only storage + audit trail) before they’ll run any inference. Sales (grace) wants this folded into public v1. Need a rapid scope tradeoff.

jordan: Engineering reality: end-to-end residency + exportable audit logs touches storage tier, ingest pipeline, and compliance hooks. Ballpark 2w infra + 3 days compliance pipeline + testing. Could be parallel but it's not zero-risk.

grace: Sales: CuraTech is a high-signal customer and a case study in healthcare vertical. Theyre willing to sign a paid pilot if we can commit to residency guarantees, but theyre also clear they prefer it GA.

sam: From UX/Docs: we can add explicit residency labels in the onboarding flow and a customer-facing note about EU-only storage quickly (~3 days) but we cant fake an audit pack.

lee: Ops: we can run a hosted EU tenant for 1 pilot manually (provisioning, export snapshots) for a few weeks, but that requires runbook and on-call support. Not sustainable for many customers.

maya: Options: (A) Keep public v1 narrow (no residency guarantee) and offer CuraTech a paid "enterprise pilot" with dedicated EU tenancy and runbook. (B) Fold residency into public v1 -> shift v1 ~2w and expand QA/compliance. (C) Ship labeled "EU-enabled" experimental option in v1 behind a gated rollout; deliver audit evidence later. Thoughts?

jordan: Prefers A. It isolates schedule risk and we can scope infra work as a separate deliverable. C still forces immediate compliance work and testing. B shifts everything.

grace: Sales will try A first (paid pilot) but flags risk: if CuraTech insists on GA date, churn risk increases. I can negotiate SOW with a residency SLA + pilot fee.

sam: If we pick A, UX can ship the residency labeling + a migration doc to make onboarding clear.

lee: If A chosen, ops needs a short runbook and timeboxed SLA in the SOW stating how long we support manual tenancy before automating.

maya: Draft quick checklist: 
```
Public v1 (baseline):
- core inference API
- simple tenant routing (api-key per tenant)
- telemetry + canary rollout

Enterprise pilot (residency SOW):
- dedicated EU tenant for CuraTech (manual ops for pilot)
- exportable audit trail delivered as part of SOW
- runbook + defined support window (ops SLA)
- timeline for GA residency feature (v1.1) and acceptance criteria
```

jordan: Il write a concise RFC outlining infra work and a minimal automated residency plan (estimate + risks) by EOD tomorrow.

sam: Il prepare the onboarding label + migration doc and a short FAQ for sales by Wed.

grace: Il surface SOW option to CuraTech and report back by EOD tomorrow.

lee: Ops-bot, please add a planning slot for "CuraTech pilot runbook" next week.

ops-bot: Calendar event created: "CuraTech residency pilot planning" 2026-04-01 10:00 PT. Invite: @maya @jordan @sam @lee @grace.

maya: Quick vote: react :thumbsup: to keep v1 date + run pilot SOW, :thumbsdown: to fold residency into v1 and delay.

jordan: :thumbsup:

sam: :thumbsup:

lee: :thumbsup: (ops ok for timeboxed pilot)

grace: :thumbsup: (sales will push SOW first)

maya: Consensus = keep v1 and pursue enterprise pilot SOW for residency. Il update the milestone tracker after jordan's RFC. Thanks team.
